name: Voyager 1
status_summary: Actively communicating from interstellar space over 165 AU (~24.7 billion km) from Earth. In 2024, NASA engineers successfully resolved a telemetry memory synchronization issue, keeping its science instruments transmitting.
mission_purpose: Originally designed to explore Jupiter and Saturn and their rings and moons. Following its primary mission, it embarked on the Voyager Interstellar Mission to characterize the outer boundaries of the heliosphere and interstellar space.
historical_significance: The farthest human-made object from Earth and the first machine to cross the heliopause into interstellar space (August 25, 2012). Carries the famous Golden Record containing sounds and images of Earth.
power_source: Radioisotope Thermoelectric Generators (MHW-RTG) powered by Plutonium-238

instruments.name: Triaxial Fluxgate Magnetometer
instruments.purpose_student_friendly: Measures changes in magnetic fields in deep space, revealing when the probe exited our Sun's magnetic bubble.
instruments.technical_description: High and low-field triaxial fluxgate sensors measuring interstellar magnetic field vectors and turbulence.

instruments.name: Cosmic Ray Subsystem
instruments.purpose_student_friendly: Counts high-energy particles from exploding stars and interstellar space.
instruments.technical_description: High-energy and low-energy telescope systems detecting electrons, protons, and cosmic ray nuclei.

instruments.name: Low-Energy Charged Particle Instrument
instruments.purpose_student_friendly: Detects solar wind particles and cosmic rays flowing around the spacecraft.
instruments.technical_description: Solid-state detector system mounted on a stepping motor assessing energy spectrum and directional distribution.

milestones.title: Launch from Cape Canaveral
milestones.description: Voyager 1 launched aboard a Titan IIIE rocket, embarking on the historic Grand Tour of the outer planets.

milestones.title: Jupiter Closest Approach
milestones.description: Flew within 349,000 km of Jupiter's cloud tops, discovering active sulfur volcanoes on moon Io.

milestones.title: Saturn & Titan Flyby
milestones.description: Examined Saturn's ring structure and passed close to Titan, revealing its thick, opaque nitrogen atmosphere.

milestones.title: The Pale Blue Dot Portrait
milestones.description: Turned cameras back toward Earth to capture the iconic 'Family Portrait', showing Earth as a tiny speck of light in a sunbeam.

milestones.title: Entry into Interstellar Space
milestones.description: First human machine to cross the heliopause, detecting an abrupt drop in solar particles and a surge in interstellar cosmic rays.

discoveries.title: First Active Extraterrestrial Volcanoes
discoveries.plain_english_summary: Voyager 1 spotted violent volcanic eruptions on Jupiter's moon Io, proving Earth is not the only geologically active world.
discoveries.why_it_matters: Proved that tidal gravitational flexing from giant planets can heat a moon's interior, opening new frontiers in astrobiology.

discoveries.title: Mapping the Solar System's Boundary
discoveries.plain_english_summary: Discovered the exact boundary (heliopause) where the Sun's solar wind collides with matter between stars.
discoveries.why_it_matters: Helps scientists understand how our solar system is shielded from galactic cosmic radiation.

sources.title: NASA NSSDCA Master Catalog: Voyager 1
sources.quotation_or_reference: NSSDC ID: 1977-084A | Voyager 1 Primary Mission Profile

physical_fate: Drifting through the cold interstellar medium over 24.7 billion kilometers (165 AU) from Earth, travelling at 61,000 km/h toward the constellation Ophiuchus. While its cameras were turned off in 1990 to conserve nuclear power, its magnetometer and cosmic ray detectors continue transmitting scientific telemetry across the void via the Deep Space Network.
fast_facts: Carries the Golden Record: a 12-inch gold-plated copper phonograph record containing sounds, music, and greetings from Earth.
It takes over 22 hours and 50 minutes for a radio signal travelling at the speed of light to reach Earth from Voyager 1.
In 1990, Voyager 1 turned its camera back to take the iconic "Pale Blue Dot" portrait from 6 billion km away.

name: Voyager 2
status_summary: Actively transmitting science data from interstellar space over 138 AU (~20.6 billion km) from Earth. Its Plasma Science instrument remains operational, measuring interstellar medium density.
mission_purpose: Designed to conduct a grand tour of Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune using rare planetary gravitational alignment.
historical_significance: The only spacecraft in human history to visit all four giant outer planets (Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune) and the second machine to enter interstellar space.

instruments.name: Plasma Science Experiment
instruments.purpose_student_friendly: Measures the temperature, speed, and density of electrified solar gas and interstellar plasma.
instruments.technical_description: Modulated-grid Faraday cup measuring low-energy ionized particles in the range of 10 eV to 6 keV.

instruments.name: Magnetometer
instruments.purpose_student_friendly: Monitors the strength and direction of magnetic fields across the outer planets and beyond.
instruments.technical_description: Triaxial fluxgate magnetometer payload.

milestones.title: Launched Before Voyager 1
milestones.description: Launched 16 days before Voyager 1 on a longer, slower trajectory enabling visits to Uranus and Neptune.

milestones.title: Only Visit to Uranus
milestones.description: Flew within 81,500 km of Uranus, discovering 10 new moons and its tilted, off-center magnetic field.

milestones.title: Only Visit to Neptune
milestones.description: Passed 4,950 km above Neptune's north pole, discovering the Great Dark Spot and nitrogen ice geysers on moon Triton.

milestones.title: Crossed into Interstellar Space
milestones.description: Exited the heliosphere, with its working plasma detector confirming entry into cold interstellar gas.

discoveries.title: Triton's Nitrogen Geysers
discoveries.plain_english_summary: Discovered active icy geysers erupting nitrogen gas and black dust 8 kilometers into the sky on Neptune's moon Triton.
discoveries.why_it_matters: Proved that geological activity can occur in the coldest environments in the solar system (-235 deg C).

discoveries.title: Tilted Magnetic Fields of Ice Giants
discoveries.plain_english_summary: Found that Uranus and Neptune have bizarre magnetic fields tilted far away from their rotational poles.
discoveries.why_it_matters: Showed that magnetic fields can be generated in churning fluid mantles rather than deep metal cores.

sources.title: NASA JPL Voyager 2 Science & Status Archives

physical_fate: Travelling through interstellar space at 138 AU (~20.6 billion km) from Earth toward the constellation Pavo. It remains the only human machine to have visited Uranus and Neptune, with its Plasma Science detector actively tasting interstellar gas.
fast_facts: Launched 16 days before Voyager 1, taking advantage of a once-every-175-years planetary alignment.
Discovered 10 new moons at Uranus and active nitrogen ice geysers on Neptune's moon Triton.
Entered interstellar space on November 5, 2018, confirmed by its functioning plasma instrument.

name: Perseverance Rover
status_summary: Actively exploring Jezero Crater, collecting sealed Martian rock and regolith core samples for future retrieval by the Mars Sample Return mission.
mission_purpose: Seek signs of ancient microbial life, characterize Mars' past climate and geology, test oxygen generation from atmospheric CO2, and cache rock samples for Earth return.
historical_significance: Carried the Ingenuity Mars Helicopter (the first powered flight on another planet) and generated breathable oxygen on Mars using MOXIE.

instruments.name: Mastcam-Z
instruments.purpose_student_friendly: High-definition zoom cameras that act as the rover's eyes, taking 3D color panoramic photos.
instruments.technical_description: Multispectral stereoscopic imaging system with 3:1 zoom capability.

instruments.name: SuperCam
instruments.purpose_student_friendly: Fires an infrared laser at rocks from up to 7 meters away to zap them into glowing vapor and read their minerals.
instruments.technical_description: Laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy (LIBS), Raman, and time-resolved fluorescence spectroscopy with microphone.

instruments.name: Mars Oxygen ISRU Experiment
instruments.purpose_student_friendly: A technology demo that turned thin Martian carbon dioxide gas into pure, breathable oxygen like a mechanical tree.
instruments.technical_description: Solid oxide electrolysis cell generating up to 10 g/hr of O2 from atmospheric CO2.

instruments.name: Radar Imager for Mars' Subsurface Experiment
instruments.purpose_student_friendly: Ground-penetrating radar that peeks under the Martian soil up to 10 meters deep.
instruments.technical_description: Frequency-modulated continuous-wave radar operating at 150-1200 MHz.

milestones.title: Launch toward Mars
milestones.description: Lifted off from Cape Canaveral Air Force Station aboard an Atlas V rocket.

milestones.title: Touchdown in Jezero Crater
milestones.description: Executed flawless entry, descent, and landing using the legendary Sky Crane maneuver.

milestones.title: Ingenuity's First Flight
milestones.description: Scout companion Ingenuity achieved the first powered, controlled flight on another world (Wright Brothers moment).

milestones.title: First Cored Martian Rock Sample
milestones.description: Successfully drilled and hermetically sealed sample 'Montdenier' inside an ultra-clean titanium tube.

discoveries.title: Confirmation of Ancient River Delta in Jezero
discoveries.plain_english_summary: Found rounded river stones, silt layers, and clay minerals proving Jezero Crater was filled with a deep lake billions of years ago.
discoveries.why_it_matters: Ancient lakes and river deltas are the premier environments where signs of microbial life could be preserved.

discoveries.title: Oxygen Generation on Another Planet
discoveries.plain_english_summary: MOXIE demonstrated that future astronauts can manufacture their own oxygen directly from the Martian air.
discoveries.why_it_matters: Reduces the payload and cost required for human missions to Mars.

sources.title: NASA Mars 2020 Perseverance Mission Overview
sources.quotation_or_reference: Official NASA Mars 2020 Science Team Portal

operational_lifespan: Planned: 1 Mars year (~2 Earth years) | Actual: Operational since Feb 2021
physical_fate: Actively traversing and drilling in Jezero Crater, climbing the ancient river delta to collect hermetically sealed rock cores stored in sterile titanium tubes on its chassis and on the Martian surface for future return to Earth.
fast_facts: Carried the Ingenuity Mars Helicopter, which achieved 72 powered flights in Mars's thin air (designed for just 5!).
MOXIE generated 122 grams of breathable oxygen directly from Martian carbon dioxide.
Its wheels feature custom aluminum treads designed to avoid the wheel puncture wear experienced by Curiosity.

name: Curiosity Rover (MSL)
status_summary: Operating for over 14 years on Mars (over 4,300 sols), steadily climbing Mount Sharp (Aeolis Mons) to analyze rock layers that record billions of years of changing Martian climate.
mission_purpose: Assess whether Mars ever had an environment capable of supporting microbial life (planetary habitability).
historical_significance: First rover to use the revolutionary rocket-powered Sky Crane landing architecture and discovered definitive evidence of ancient freshwater lakes and organic molecules on Mars.

instruments.name: Sample Analysis at Mars
instruments.purpose_student_friendly: A chemistry laboratory inside the rover's belly that bakes rock powders to sniff for carbon-based organic molecules.
instruments.technical_description: Suite consisting of a quadrupole mass spectrometer, gas chromatograph, and tunable laser spectrometer.

instruments.name: Chemistry and Camera
instruments.purpose_student_friendly: Fires a rock-blasting laser to study rock compositions from a distance.
instruments.technical_description: Laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy paired with a remote micro-imager.

instruments.name: Chemistry and Mineralogy
instruments.purpose_student_friendly: Shines X-rays through powdered rocks to identify their exact crystal minerals.
instruments.technical_description: X-ray diffraction and fluorescence instrument.

milestones.title: Launch from Earth
milestones.description: Departed Earth on an Atlas V rocket from Space Launch Complex 41.

milestones.title: The 'Seven Minutes of Terror' Touchdown
milestones.description: Landed safely in Gale Crater via guided atmospheric entry, parachute, and rocket-powered Sky Crane.

milestones.title: Ancient Habitability Confirmed
milestones.description: Analysis of rock samples at Yellowknife Bay confirmed ancient Mars had freshwater, carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, and nitrogen.

milestones.title: Ancient Organic Molecules Detected
milestones.description: Identified diverse 3-billion-year-old organic carbon compounds in lakebed mudstones.

discoveries.title: Ancient Mars Was Habitable
discoveries.plain_english_summary: Discovered that Gale Crater once hosted calm, freshwater lakes with drinkable water and all basic chemical ingredients for life.
discoveries.why_it_matters: Proved that Mars had environmental conditions where life could have started and thrived.

discoveries.title: Methane Spikes in Martian Atmosphere
discoveries.plain_english_summary: Detected mysterious seasonal pulses of methane gas in the atmosphere that rise and fall with the Martian seasons.
discoveries.why_it_matters: Methane can be produced either by underground geological reactions or living microbes.

sources.title: NASA Mars Science Laboratory / Curiosity
sources.quotation_or_reference: JPL Curiosity Mission Archives & Science Papers

operational_lifespan: Planned: 2 years | Actual: 14+ years (over 4,300 Martian sols)
physical_fate: Steadily ascending the foothills of Mount Sharp (Aeolis Mons) inside Gale Crater, analyzing sediment layers that preserve billions of years of Martian transition from a wet lake world to a frozen desert.
fast_facts: Weighs nearly 900 kg on Earth (about the size of an SUV), but only 340 kg in Mars's lower gravity.
Uses the ChemCam laser to zap rocks up to 7 meters away, creating a spark of glowing plasma.
Celebrated its first Martian birthday in 2013 by playing "Happy Birthday" to itself using its SAM instrument frequencies.

name: Cassini-Huygens
status_summary: Concluded its legendary 13-year tour of Saturn on September 15, 2017, with an intentional 'Grand Finale' dive into Saturn's atmosphere to protect ocean moons Enceladus and Titan from potential contamination.
mission_purpose: Study Saturn, its magnificent ring systems, magnetic field, and extensive moon system in unprecedented detail.
historical_significance: Discovered subsurface global saltwater ocean and geysers on Enceladus, dropped the ESA Huygens probe onto Titan's hydrocarbon surface, and revolutionized our understanding of ocean worlds.
power_source: 3 General Purpose Heat Source Radioisotope Thermoelectric Generators (GPHS-RTG)

instruments.name: Composite Infrared Spectrometer
instruments.purpose_student_friendly: Measured heat temperatures and chemical compositions of Saturn's rings and moon surfaces.
instruments.technical_description: Dual-interferometer spectrometer operating in mid- and far-infrared wavelengths.

instruments.name: Ion and Neutral Mass Spectrometer
instruments.purpose_student_friendly: Tasted and identified molecules sprayed out of Enceladus's icy geysers.
instruments.technical_description: Quadrupole mass spectrometer analyzing neutral particles and positive ions.

instruments.name: Imaging Science Subsystem
instruments.purpose_student_friendly: High-resolution wide-angle and narrow-angle digital cameras capturing over 450,000 photos of Saturn.
instruments.technical_description: Dual CCD camera system with multiple spectral filter wheels.

milestones.title: Launch from Cape Canaveral
milestones.description: Began a 7-year voyage using gravity assists from Venus (twice), Earth, and Jupiter.

milestones.title: Saturn Orbit Insertion
milestones.description: Fired main engine to slip through Saturn's rings and become Saturn's first orbital resident.

milestones.title: Huygens Probe Titan Landing
milestones.description: ESA Huygens probe parachuted through Titan's nitrogen haze, landing on wet hydrocarbon pebbles.

milestones.title: Enceladus Geysers Discovered
milestones.description: Flew through giant plumes of water vapor and organic molecules erupting from Enceladus's south pole.

milestones.title: The Grand Finale Plunge
milestones.description: Dived straight into Saturn's atmosphere, transmitting real-time composition data until vaporization.

discoveries.title: Global Subsurface Saltwater Ocean on Enceladus
discoveries.plain_english_summary: Discovered that tiny moon Enceladus has a warm saltwater ocean beneath its ice crust with hydrothermal vents.
discoveries.why_it_matters: Enceladus has water, energy, and organic molecules, making it one of the premier locations to search for life.

discoveries.title: Liquid Methane Lakes and Rain on Titan
discoveries.plain_english_summary: Revealed that Titan has a complete hydrological cycle like Earth, but with liquid methane and ethane instead of water.
discoveries.why_it_matters: Demonstrated that planetary weather and lakes can exist under exotic cryogenic chemistry.

sources.title: NASA Cassini-Huygens Mission Archive
sources.quotation_or_reference: Cassini Legacy Press Kit & Science Summary

operational_lifespan: Planned: 4 years at Saturn | Actual: 13 years (2004–2017)
physical_fate: Vaporized high in Saturn's swirling hydrogen-helium atmosphere on September 15, 2017, at 120,000 km/h. Ground controllers executed this sacrificial dive to ensure the spent spacecraft could never accidentally crash into and contaminate pristine ocean moons Enceladus or Titan.
fast_facts: Discovered that tiny moon Enceladus shoots plumes of saltwater ice and organic molecules from deep hydrothermal vents.
Dropped the European Space Agency's Huygens probe through Titan's orange haze onto a riverbed of water-ice pebbles and liquid methane.
Orbited Saturn 294 times and snapped over 450,000 breathtaking photographs.

name: New Horizons
status_summary: Actively cruising through the distant Kuiper Belt over 59 AU from the Sun, measuring the interstellar boundary, dust environment, and observing distant Kuiper Belt objects.
mission_purpose: Conduct the first reconnaissance of the Pluto system and explore the ancient relics of the Kuiper Belt.
historical_significance: Fastest spacecraft ever launched from Earth at departure (16.26 km/s); transformed Pluto from an indistinct dot into an active world of nitrogen glaciers and mountain ranges.

instruments.name: Long Range Reconnaissance Imager
instruments.purpose_student_friendly: A giant telephoto camera telescope that captured the sharpest photos of Pluto and Arrokoth.
instruments.technical_description: 20.8 cm aperture Ritchey-Chrétien reflector with 1024x1024 back-illuminated CCD.

instruments.name: Solar Wind Around Pluto
instruments.purpose_student_friendly: Measures how the Sun's particle wind interacts with Pluto's escaping atmosphere and distant space.
instruments.technical_description: Electrostatic analyzer and retarding potential analyzer measuring ions up to 7.5 keV.

milestones.title: High-Speed Departure from Earth
milestones.description: Blasted into space on an Atlas V with a Star-48B third stage, reaching the Moon's orbit in just 9 hours.

milestones.title: Jupiter Gravity Assist
milestones.description: Swung past Jupiter, gaining 14,000 km/h in velocity and capturing stunning photos of Io's volcano Tvashtar.

milestones.title: Historic Pluto Flyby
milestones.description: Flew 12,500 km above Pluto, revealing its heart-shaped nitrogen ice glacier Tombaugh Regio.

milestones.title: Flyby of Contact Binary Arrokoth
milestones.description: Explored Arrokoth (4 billion km from Earth), the most primitive primordial object ever observed up close.

discoveries.title: Pluto's Beating Heart of Convecting Nitrogen Ice
discoveries.plain_english_summary: Discovered Sputnik Planitia: a 1,000-km glacier of nitrogen ice that constantly bubbles and renews itself like a lava lamp.
discoveries.why_it_matters: Demonstrated that small frozen worlds in the outer solar system can remain geologically dynamic.

discoveries.title: Planetary Genesis Revealed by Arrokoth
discoveries.plain_english_summary: Arrokoth proved that planets coalesced gently from clouds of pebbles rather than violent high-speed collisions.
discoveries.why_it_matters: Solved a multi-decade debate in planetary physics regarding planetesimal formation.

sources.title: NASA JHUAPL New Horizons Mission Portal
sources.quotation_or_reference: New Horizons Science Payload & Kuiper Belt Observations

operational_lifespan: Planned: 10 years | Actual: 20+ years (operational in Kuiper Belt)
physical_fate: Cruising past 59 AU from the Sun through the outer Kuiper Belt, observing the outer heliophysics environment and measuring cosmic background light from beyond the dust glow of our inner solar system.
fast_facts: Carried a thimble-sized container of the ashes of Clyde Tombaugh, the astronomer who discovered Pluto in 1930.
Fastest spacecraft ever launched from Earth at separation: 58,536 km/h (reached the Moon in just 9 hours).
Discovered that Pluto has active nitrogen glaciers that flow and circulate like a lava lamp.

name: InSight Lander
status_summary: Mission officially concluded on December 21, 2022, after thick Martian dust accumulated on its solar arrays, depleting electrical power. Successfully completed its primary and extended science investigations.
mission_purpose: Study the deep interior of Mars using seismology, geodesy, and heat transport to understand how rocky planets formed.
historical_significance: Placed the first ultra-sensitive seismometer directly on the surface of Mars, detecting over 1,300 'marsquakes' and mapping the Martian crust, mantle, and molten liquid iron core.

instruments.name: Seismic Experiment for Interior Structure
instruments.purpose_student_friendly: A super-sensitive digital ear placed on the ground inside a vacuum dome that heard subterranean vibrations and quakes.
instruments.technical_description: Six-sensor seismometer covering ultra-broadband (0.01 to 10 Hz) and short-period (0.1 to 50 Hz) seismic waves.

instruments.name: Heat Flow and Physical Properties Package
instruments.purpose_student_friendly: A mechanical mole nicknamed the 'Mole' designed to burrow into soil to measure planet heat.
instruments.technical_description: Self-hammering penetrator with thermal conductivity sensors.

milestones.title: Launch from Vandenberg
milestones.description: First interplanetary launch from the U.S. West Coast.

milestones.title: Smooth Landing on Elysium Planitia
milestones.description: Landed safely on a flat, smooth lava plain chosen for safe instrument deployment.

milestones.title: First Ever Marsquake Detected
milestones.description: SEIS recorded the first verified seismic rumble originating from within the planet.

milestones.title: Final Signal to Earth
milestones.description: Transmitted its poignant final photograph and telemetry before battery voltage dropped below operational threshold.

discoveries.title: Mars Has a Large, Liquid Core
discoveries.plain_english_summary: By listening to bouncing quake echoes, InSight measured Mars' core: a molten sphere of iron and sulfur ~3,660 km across.
discoveries.why_it_matters: Helps planetary scientists understand why Mars lost its protective magnetic field billions of years ago.

sources.title: NASA InSight Mission End Summary
sources.quotation_or_reference: InSight Telemetry Archive & Mission Closeout Report

physical_fate: Resting silently on the flat lava plain of Elysium Planitia on Mars. Its solar arrays are thickly blanketed by reddish atmospheric dust, which gradually starved its batteries of power until final contact on December 15, 2022.
fast_facts: Detected over 1,300 marsquakes using its ultra-sensitive French seismometer (SEIS).
Proved that Mars has a surprisingly large molten iron-sulfur core approximately 3,660 km across.
Its robotic arm picked up a heavy wind-and-thermal shield and placed it carefully over the seismometer on the Martian soil.

name: Opportunity Rover (MER-B)
status_summary: Operated for nearly 15 years (designed for 90 days), driving 45.16 km across Mars. In June 2018, a catastrophic planet-encircling dust storm blocked sunlight to its solar arrays; NASA officially concluded the mission on Feb 13, 2019.
mission_purpose: Search for geological clues regarding past water activity on Mars.
historical_significance: Holds the off-world driving record (over a marathon distance of 45.16 km) and discovered hematite 'blueberries', providing the first definitive ground truth that liquid water soaked ancient Mars.
power_source: Solar cell arrays generating up to 140 W

instruments.name: Panoramic Camera
instruments.purpose_student_friendly: High-mounted stereo cameras that captured 3D landscapes and rock textures.
instruments.technical_description: Multispectral stereo camera system.

instruments.name: Miniature Thermal Emission Spectrometer
instruments.purpose_student_friendly: Infrared instrument that diagnosed rock minerals from a distance.
instruments.technical_description: Fourier transform infrared spectrometer.

instruments.name: Rock Abrasion Tool
instruments.purpose_student_friendly: A mechanical diamond-grit grinder that ground through outer weathered rock crust to expose fresh minerals.
instruments.technical_description: Precision diamond-toothed cutting wheel grinding circular pits 45 mm diameter.

milestones.title: Launch toward Mars
milestones.description: Lifted off from Cape Canaveral atop a Boeing Delta II Heavy.

milestones.title: Interplanetary Hole-in-One Landing
milestones.description: Bounced down encased in airbags directly inside Eagle Crater in Meridiani Planum.

milestones.title: Completed Off-Earth Marathon
milestones.description: Passed 42.195 km of total driving distance on Mars, completing an Olympic marathon.

milestones.title: Final Transmission
milestones.description: Transmitted its last signal as dust skies darkened over Perseverance Valley.

discoveries.title: Hematite Blueberries (Liquid Water Proof)
discoveries.plain_english_summary: Discovered billions of tiny gray spherules dubbed 'blueberries' made of hematite mineral formed in acidic groundwater.
discoveries.why_it_matters: Proved without doubt that water soaked and flowed through ancient Martian soils.

sources.title: NASA NSSDCA: Mars Exploration Rover - Opportunity

operational_lifespan: Planned: 90 Martian days | Actual: 14.5 years (5,111 sols)
physical_fate: Resting in Perseverance Valley on the rim of Endeavour Crater on Mars. In June 2018, a catastrophic global dust storm darkened the sky for months, cutting off sunlight to its solar arrays; NASA officially concluded the mission on February 13, 2019.
fast_facts: Holds the off-world driving record: 45.16 kilometers (more than an Olympic marathon).
Discovered "blueberries" (tiny hematite spheres) that proved liquid water once flowed across ancient Mars.
Survived over 55 times its design lifetime thanks to unexpected Martian dust-cleaning wind gusts.

name: Apollo 11 Lunar Module (Eagle) — Descent Stage
status_summary: Rests permanently at Tranquility Base (0.67408 deg N, 23.47297 deg E) on the Moon. High-resolution orbital photography by NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) in 2009 and 2012 confirmed the descent stage, scientific equipment (EASEP), and astronaut footpaths remain undisturbed in the lunar vacuum.
mission_purpose: Achieve the national goal set by President John F. Kennedy of landing humans on the Moon and returning them safely to Earth.
historical_significance: The historic first human landing on another celestial body (July 20, 1969). The Descent Stage remains an immortal monument to human exploration and engineering.

instruments.name: Early Apollo Surface Experiments Package
instruments.purpose_student_friendly: First science kit placed on the Moon, containing a moonquake sensor and laser reflector.
instruments.technical_description: Included Passive Seismic Experiment Package (PSEP) and Lunar Ranging Retroreflector (LRRR).

instruments.name: Lunar Ranging Retroreflector
instruments.purpose_student_friendly: A special prism mirror that bounces lasers fired from Earth back to measure the exact distance to the Moon.
instruments.technical_description: Array of 100 quartz corner-cube prisms that continue to be targeted by Earth observatories today.

milestones.title: Launch of Apollo 11
milestones.description: Saturn V rocket lifted off from Kennedy Space Center carrying Armstrong, Aldrin, and Collins.

milestones.title: 'The Eagle Has Landed'
milestones.description: Touched down in the Sea of Tranquility with less than 30 seconds of fuel remaining.

milestones.title: First Steps on the Moon
milestones.description: Neil Armstrong descended the ladder: 'That's one small step for man, one giant leap for mankind.'

milestones.title: Lunar Liftoff
milestones.description: The Ascent Stage fired its engine to rendezvous with Columbia, leaving the Descent Stage behind forever.

discoveries.title: The Moon Is Slowly Drifting Away from Earth
discoveries.plain_english_summary: By bouncing lasers off the Apollo 11 reflector, scientists proved the Moon recedes from Earth at 3.8 cm per year.
discoveries.why_it_matters: Provides crucial data on tidal friction, Earth's rotational slowing, and orbital dynamics.

sources.title: NASA Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) Apollo 11 Site Confirmation
sources.quotation_or_reference: LRO Narrow Angle Camera (NAC) Feature: Tranquility Base Coordinates Confirmed

operational_lifespan: Planned: 2.5 days on lunar surface | Actual: Preserved permanently
physical_fate: Rests permanently at Tranquility Base (0.67408° N, 23.47297° E) on the Moon. In the airless lunar vacuum with no wind, rain, or erosion, the gold-foil descent stage, astronaut bootprints, and scientific equipment remain in pristine condition millions of years into the future.
fast_facts: Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin landed with less than 30 seconds of fuel remaining in the descent engine tank.
Its Laser Ranging Retroreflector continues to be targeted by lasers from Earth today, proving the Moon recedes 3.8 cm per year.
Carries a stainless steel plaque signed by the three astronauts and President Nixon: "Here men from the planet Earth first set foot upon the Moon. We came in peace for all mankind."

name: Juno
status_summary: Actively performing close elliptical polar flybys (perijoves) of Jupiter and close encounters with moons Ganymede, Europa, and volcanic Io in its extended science mission.
mission_purpose: Understand the origin and evolution of Jupiter, map its magnetic and gravitational fields, and measure atmospheric water content.
historical_significance: Farthest solar-powered spacecraft in history; penetrated Jupiter's radiation belts to reveal that Jupiter has a fuzzy, diluted core and deep atmospheric roots.
power_source: Three 9-meter solar array panels generating ~500 W at Jupiter

instruments.name: Microwave Radiometer
instruments.purpose_student_friendly: Peers through the thick upper clouds to measure deep water and ammonia levels.
instruments.technical_description: Six-frequency radiometer operating from 600 MHz to 22 GHz.

instruments.name: Jovian Auroral Distributions Experiment
instruments.purpose_student_friendly: Measures the particles creating Jupiter's colossal glowing polar auroras.
instruments.technical_description: Set of three electron sensors and an energetic ion mass spectrometer.

instruments.name: JunoCam
instruments.purpose_student_friendly: Color visible-light camera engaging students and public scientists to process raw images of storms.
instruments.technical_description: Push-frame four-filter visible light camera.

milestones.title: Launch from Cape Canaveral
milestones.description: Began a 5-year journey across the inner solar system.

milestones.title: Jupiter Orbit Insertion
milestones.description: Fired main engine on Fourth of July to enter Jupiter's punishing polar radiation orbit.

milestones.title: Closest Flyby of Moon Ganymede
milestones.description: Passed within 1,038 km of Ganymede, the solar system's largest moon.

milestones.title: Close Flyby of Volcanic Moon Io
milestones.description: Flew within 1,500 km of Io, snapping spectacular photos of magma lakes and active plumes.

discoveries.title: Jupiter Has a 'Diluted' Fuzzy Core
discoveries.plain_english_summary: Gravity data proved Jupiter does not have a solid rock core, but a giant, fuzzy core mixed with metallic hydrogen.
discoveries.why_it_matters: Suggests young Jupiter suffered an enormous head-on collision with a protoplanet in its infancy.

operational_lifespan: Planned: 2 years | Actual: 15+ years (operational polar orbiter)
physical_fate: Actively performing close elliptical passes (perijoves) through Jupiter's hazardous radiation belts, skimming thousands of kilometers above its ammonia clouds and conducting historic close flybys of moons Ganymede, Europa, and volcanic Io.
fast_facts: Farthest solar-powered spacecraft in history, generating electricity with three 9-meter solar array wings even 800 million km from the Sun.
Carries a titanium radiation vault with 1-cm thick walls to protect its sensitive computer brain from Jupiter's lethal magnetic radiation.
Carries three aluminum LEGO figurines representing the Roman god Jupiter, his wife Juno, and the astronomer Galileo Galilei.

name: Parker Solar Probe
status_summary: Actively 'touching the Sun' during recurring close perihelion passes. In its final planned orbits, it swoops within 6.1 million km of the solar surface at mind-boggling speeds exceeding 690,000 km/h.
mission_purpose: Trace the flow of energy that heats the solar corona and accelerates the supersonic solar wind.
historical_significance: The fastest human-made object in history, the closest machine to the Sun, and the first NASA spacecraft named after a living scientist (Dr. Eugene Parker). Protected by an 11.4 cm carbon-composite heat shield that endures 1,400 deg C.

instruments.name: FIELDS
instruments.purpose_student_friendly: Measures electric and magnetic fields and waves in the sizzling solar corona.
instruments.technical_description: Five voltage sensors, two fluxgate magnetometers, and a search-coil magnetometer.

instruments.name: Solar Wind Electrons Alphas and Protons
instruments.purpose_student_friendly: Directly scoops up particles flowing off the Sun to measure velocity and temperature.
instruments.technical_description: Solar Probe Cup (Faraday cup) and two electrostatic analyzers.

instruments.name: Wide-Field Imager for Solar Probe
instruments.purpose_student_friendly: Telescopic cameras taking 3D photos of solar wind coronal mass ejections.
instruments.technical_description: Dual optical telescopes protected behind the heat shield.

milestones.title: Launch into Deep Space
milestones.description: Launched aboard a Delta IV Heavy with a Star 48BV upper stage.

milestones.title: First Time 'Touching the Sun'
milestones.description: Passed inside the Alfven critical surface, officially flying directly through the Sun's upper atmosphere.

milestones.title: Record Closest Approach (6.1 Million km)
milestones.description: Completed historic Venus flybys to slingshot into its record-breaking closest perihelion pass.

discoveries.title: Magnetic 'Switchbacks' in Solar Wind
discoveries.plain_english_summary: Discovered that magnetic fields in the solar wind violently flip direction like S-shaped zigzags, releasing explosive energy.
discoveries.why_it_matters: Solves the mystery of why the solar corona is hundreds of times hotter than the surface of the Sun.

sources.title: NASA Parker Solar Probe Mission Overview
sources.quotation_or_reference: NSSDC ID: 2018-065A | Parker Solar Probe Science Team

sources.title: JHUAPL Parker Solar Probe Science Operations
sources.quotation_or_reference: Parker Solar Probe Telemetry & Science Instruments

operational_lifespan: Planned: 7 years | Actual: Operational since Aug 2018
physical_fate: Repeatedly diving deep into the Sun's blazing outer corona. Protected behind an 11.4 cm carbon-composite heat shield that endures temperatures of 1,400°C while its instruments remain at comfortable room temperature (30°C).
fast_facts: The fastest human-made object in history, reaching speeds exceeding 690,000 km/h (fast enough to fly from New York to Tokyo in under a minute!).
Officially "touched the Sun" on April 28, 2021, by crossing inside the Alfvén critical boundary.
The first NASA spacecraft named after a living scientist: solar astrophysicist Dr. Eugene Parker.

name: Pioneer 10
status_summary: Drifting silently on an interstellar trajectory out of the solar system toward the red giant star Aldebaran in the constellation Taurus. The last faint signal was received on January 23, 2003, when its nuclear generator could no longer power the transmitter.
mission_purpose: First mission to transit the dangerous asteroid belt and make direct observations of Jupiter.
historical_significance: First spacecraft to traverse the Asteroid Belt and first to fly past Jupiter (Dec 3, 1973). Carries the iconic gold-anodized Pioneer Plaque depicting human figures and our solar system's address.

instruments.name: Helium Vector Magnetometer
instruments.purpose_student_friendly: Measured Jupiter's colossal magnetic field for the first time.
instruments.technical_description: Helium gas discharge cell measuring magnetic fields up to 140,000 gamma.

instruments.name: Geiger Tube Telescope
instruments.purpose_student_friendly: Counted electrons and protons in Jupiter's radiation belts.
instruments.technical_description: Seven miniature Geiger-Mueller tubes.

milestones.title: Launch from Cape Canaveral
milestones.description: Lifted off on an Atlas-Centaur, becoming the fastest human object up to that date.

milestones.title: Entering the Asteroid Belt
milestones.description: First spacecraft to enter the asteroid belt, proving it was safe to navigate without collisions.

milestones.title: Historic Jupiter Flyby
milestones.description: Flew within 130,000 km of Jupiter, obtaining first close-up images of the Great Red Spot.

milestones.title: Final Signal Received on Earth
milestones.description: NASA's Deep Space Network in Madrid detected the final whisper from 12 billion km away.

discoveries.title: Asteroid Belt Navigation Safety
discoveries.plain_english_summary: Showed that the Asteroid Belt is mostly empty vacuum rather than a dense wall of space debris.
discoveries.why_it_matters: Cleared the way for all future robotic exploration of the outer solar system.

operational_lifespan: Planned: 21 months | Actual: 30+ years of active telemetry
physical_fate: Drifting silently on an interstellar trajectory out of our solar system toward the red giant star Aldebaran in the constellation Taurus. It will take approximately 2 million years to reach the vicinity of the star. Its final faint signal was detected on January 23, 2003.
fast_facts: First human spacecraft to traverse the dangerous Asteroid Belt, proving it is mostly empty space.
First spacecraft to obtain close-up images of Jupiter and its Great Red Spot in December 1973.
Carries an iconic gold-anodized aluminum plaque depicting a man, a woman, and a pulsar map revealing Earth's cosmic address.

name: Pioneer 11
status_summary: Travelling silently into interstellar space heading generally toward the constellation Scutum. Telemetry communications ended on September 30, 1995, due to exhaustion of electrical power.
mission_purpose: Study Jupiter and perform the first historic flyby of Saturn and its rings.
historical_significance: First spacecraft to fly past Saturn (Sept 1, 1979), discovering Saturn's F-ring and paving the pathway for the Voyager spacecraft.

instruments.name: Fluxgate Magnetometer
instruments.purpose_student_friendly: Measured Saturn's magnetic field strength.
instruments.technical_description: Single-axis fluxgate magnetometer.

milestones.title: Launch from Cape Canaveral
milestones.description: Began journey toward Jupiter and Saturn.

milestones.title: Jupiter Gravitational Slingshot
milestones.description: Used Jupiter's gravity to fling it toward Saturn.

milestones.title: First Ever Saturn Flyby
milestones.description: Flew within 21,000 km of Saturn's cloud tops, discovering its narrow F-ring.

milestones.title: End of Communications
milestones.description: Final mission telemetry received by NASA DSN.

discoveries.title: Saturn's F-Ring Discovery
discoveries.plain_english_summary: Discovered Saturn's thin outer F-ring, held together by tiny shepherd moons.
discoveries.why_it_matters: Proved that gravitational shepherd moons shape and confine ring systems.

operational_lifespan: Planned: 2 years | Actual: 22 years of telemetry (1973–1995)
physical_fate: Cruising silently through interstellar space in the general direction of the constellation Scutum. Telemetry communications permanently ceased on September 30, 1995, after its nuclear generator power degraded below transmitter limits.
fast_facts: First spacecraft in human history to fly past Saturn, skimming within 21,000 km of its cloud tops on September 1, 1979.
Discovered Saturn's narrow outer F-ring and confirmed that Saturn has a strong magnetic field.
Paved the safe pathway through Saturn's rings for the subsequent Voyager 1 and 2 spacecraft.

name: Galileo
status_summary: Concluded its 14-year mission with a deliberate dive into Jupiter's atmosphere on September 21, 2003, at 173,700 km/h to prevent any possibility of crashing into and contaminating Europa's subsurface ocean.
mission_purpose: First dedicated orbiter of Jupiter and deployed the first atmospheric descent probe into a gas giant.
historical_significance: Discovered evidence of a subsurface liquid ocean on Europa and volcanic activity on Io; observed Comet Shoemaker-Levy 9 smashing into Jupiter.

instruments.name: Galileo Atmospheric Entry Probe
instruments.purpose_student_friendly: A heat-shielded capsule that parachuted into Jupiter's raging clouds to measure storms directly.
instruments.technical_description: Descent probe with neutral mass spectrometer, nephelometer, and net flux radiometer.

instruments.name: Solid State Imaging
instruments.purpose_student_friendly: Camera that snapped close-ups of Jupiter's ice moons.
instruments.technical_description: 800x800 pixel CCD with 8-position filter wheel.

milestones.title: Deployed from Space Shuttle Atlantis
milestones.description: Released from Atlantis's cargo bay and propelled by an Inertial Upper Stage.

milestones.title: Jupiter Orbit & Probe Entry
milestones.description: Atmospheric probe survived 61 minutes inside Jupiter's clouds while the orbiter began its orbital tour.

milestones.title: Final Dive into Jupiter
milestones.description: Deliberately guided into Jupiter's crushing atmosphere to safeguard Europa.

discoveries.title: Subsurface Saltwater Ocean on Europa
discoveries.plain_english_summary: Induced magnetic field measurements revealed a salty global ocean hidden beneath Europa's icy shell.
discoveries.why_it_matters: Transformed Europa into one of the top targets in the search for extraterrestrial life.

sources.title: NASA JPL Galileo Legacy Archive
sources.quotation_or_reference: JPL Galileo Jupiter Tour Science Summary

operational_lifespan: Planned: 2 years at Jupiter | Actual: 14 years (1989–2003)
physical_fate: Deliberately guided into a high-speed dive into Jupiter's crushing atmosphere on September 21, 2003, at 173,700 km/h. Like Cassini at Saturn, Galileo was intentionally vaporized to protect Europa's subsurface ocean from any risk of biological contamination.
fast_facts: Carried the first descent probe to enter the atmosphere of a gas giant planet, surviving 61 minutes under crushing pressures.
Discovered that Jupiter's icy moon Europa hides a global liquid saltwater ocean beneath its cracked ice crust.
Observed Comet Shoemaker-Levy 9 smashing violently into Jupiter's night side in July 1994.

name: Viking 1 (Lander)
status_summary: Rests permanently on Chryse Planitia. Operated for over 6 years (2,245 sols) until communication accidentally ceased on November 13, 1982, when a software command from Earth inadvertently overwrote antenna pointing instructions.
mission_purpose: Obtain high-resolution imagery of Mars, characterize surface composition, and conduct first automated biology experiments.
historical_significance: First American spacecraft to safely touch down on Mars and complete its mission, transmitting the historic first clear photographs from the Martian surface.

instruments.name: Biology Instrument Suite
instruments.purpose_student_friendly: Miniature automated biology test lab searching for microbial respiration.
instruments.technical_description: Gas Exchange, Labeled Release, and Pyrolytic Release experiments.

instruments.name: Facsimile Cameras
instruments.purpose_student_friendly: Scanning mirror cameras that revealed red rocks and a salmon-colored sky.
instruments.technical_description: Dual scanning facsimile cameras.

milestones.title: Launch toward Mars
milestones.description: Lifted off from Launch Complex 41 on a Titan IIIE.

milestones.title: Historic Landing on Mars
milestones.description: Landed safely on Chryse Planitia on the 7th anniversary of Apollo 11.

milestones.title: Last Telemetry Received
milestones.description: Final transmission received before communication link was lost.

discoveries.title: First High-Resolution Color Photos of Martian Soil
discoveries.plain_english_summary: Revealed a dry, cratered desert of rusty iron-oxide dust under a pinkish atmosphere.
discoveries.why_it_matters: Dispelled centuries of science fiction speculation about Martian vegetation and canals.

physical_fate: Rests permanently on the rocky desert plain of Chryse Planitia on Mars. Transmitted the historic first clear photographs from the Martian surface until November 13, 1982, when an antenna pointing software command inadvertently severed communication.
fast_facts: First American spacecraft to safely land on Mars and complete its mission.
Carried a robotic scoop that dug into the red Martian soil to conduct the first automated biological metabolism tests on another planet.
Its companion Viking 1 Orbiter took over 50,000 photos, mapping 97% of the Martian globe.

name: MESSENGER
status_summary: Concluded its four-year orbital mission on April 30, 2015. Because Mercury has no atmosphere to burn up in, the propellant-depleted spacecraft was guided into an intentional high-speed surface impact at 14,000 km/h, excavating an estimated 16-meter crater.
mission_purpose: Map the entire surface of Mercury, analyze its magnetic field, and investigate polar craters.
historical_significance: First spacecraft to ever orbit Mercury; revolutionized our understanding of the innermost planet.
power_source: Gallium Arsenide solar array panels with ceramic cloth sunshade

instruments.name: Mercury Dual Imaging System
instruments.purpose_student_friendly: High-definition wide-angle and narrow-angle cameras that mapped 100% of Mercury.
instruments.technical_description: Multispectral CCD camera system on a pivoting platform.

instruments.name: Neutron Spectrometer
instruments.purpose_student_friendly: Measured hydrogen atoms in polar craters to detect water ice.
instruments.technical_description: Scintillation detector measuring thermal, epithermal, and fast neutrons.

milestones.title: Launch from Cape Canaveral
milestones.description: Began complex 6.6-year cruise through inner solar system.

milestones.title: First Orbit Insertion at Mercury
milestones.description: First spacecraft to successfully enter orbit around Mercury.

milestones.title: Surface Impact
milestones.description: Impacted Mercury's northern polar region, creating a new crater estimated at 16 meters across.

discoveries.title: Abundant Water Ice in Polar Craters
discoveries.plain_english_summary: Confirmed billions of tons of water ice hidden inside permanently shadowed craters at Mercury's scorching poles.
discoveries.why_it_matters: Proved that water ice can survive even on the closest planet to the Sun.

image_attribution: NASA / JHUAPL / Carnegie Institution of Washington
operational_lifespan: Planned: 1 year in orbit | Actual: Over 4 years (2011–2015)
physical_fate: Impacted the solid rocky surface of Mercury at 14,000 km/h on April 30, 2015, on the planet's northern volcanic plains. Because Mercury has no atmosphere to burn up in, the propellant-exhausted spacecraft excavated a new impact crater estimated at 16 meters wide.
fast_facts: First spacecraft to ever orbit the Sun's innermost planet, completing 4,105 orbits.
Discovered billions of tons of water ice hidden in permanently shadowed, freezing polar craters.
Protected from the searing 430°C solar glare by a ceramic cloth sunshade.

name: Magellan
status_summary: Concluded its mission on October 13, 1994, when ground controllers commanded it to plunge into Venus's dense carbon dioxide atmosphere during Project Windmill, collecting atmospheric drag data until vaporization.
mission_purpose: Map 98% of Venus's surface through its thick cloud cover using synthetic aperture radar at high resolution.
historical_significance: First planetary spacecraft launched from a Space Shuttle. Revolutionized planetary geology by proving Venus has a relatively young volcanic surface with towering shield volcanoes and extensive lava rivers.

instruments.name: Synthetic Aperture Radar
instruments.purpose_student_friendly: Pierced through Venus's impenetrable acid clouds using radar waves to draw razor-sharp surface maps.
instruments.technical_description: S-band radar operating at 2.385 GHz creating radar swaths with 75-120 meter resolution.

instruments.name: Radar Altimeter
instruments.purpose_student_friendly: Measured the exact elevation of mountains and craters like a space tape measure.
instruments.technical_description: Nadir-pointing radar altimeter measuring surface topography to 30 meter vertical precision.

milestones.title: Deployed from Shuttle Atlantis
milestones.description: First planetary spacecraft released from a Space Shuttle cargo bay.

milestones.title: Venus Orbit Insertion
milestones.description: Fired solid rocket motor to enter polar elliptical orbit around Venus.

milestones.title: Project Windmill Atmospheric Entry
milestones.description: Guided into the upper atmosphere to measure aerodynamic torque before destruction.

discoveries.title: Venusian Surface Dominated by Volcanism
discoveries.plain_english_summary: Discovered that 85% of Venus is covered in volcanic basalt plains with hundreds of giant shield volcanoes and molten pancake domes.
discoveries.why_it_matters: Revealed how rocky planets evolve geologically without Earth-like plate tectonics.

sources.title: NASA JPL Magellan Venus Mission Archives
sources.quotation_or_reference: JPL Magellan Mission Summary & Radar Datasets

physical_fate: Guided into Venus's dense, crushing carbon dioxide atmosphere on October 13, 1994, during "Project Windmill", transmitting aerodynamic drag and upper-atmosphere data before vaporizing.
fast_facts: First planetary spacecraft deployed from the Space Shuttle cargo bay (Atlantis, STS-30).
Used Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) to penetrate thick sulfuric acid clouds, mapping 98% of Venus.
Revealed that 85% of Venus is covered in volcanic basalt plains with hundreds of giant shield volcanoes.

name: Hubble Space Telescope
status_summary: Operating in low Earth orbit (~535 km altitude) for over 36 years. Continues delivering breakthrough astronomical observations following five astronaut servicing missions.
mission_purpose: Gather ultra-sharp optical, ultraviolet, and near-infrared images of planets, stars, and distant galaxies free from Earth's atmospheric distortion.
historical_significance: One of the most transformative scientific instruments ever built; measured the age and expansion rate of the universe and proved supermassive black holes exist at galaxy centers.
power_source: Two 25-foot solar arrays generating ~2,800 W with nickel-hydrogen batteries

instruments.name: Wide Field Camera 3
instruments.purpose_student_friendly: The telescope's primary high-resolution camera, taking dazzling wide-angle color photos across optical, UV, and infrared light.
instruments.technical_description: Panchromatic camera spanning 200 nm to 1700 nm wavelengths.

instruments.name: Cosmic Origins Spectrograph
instruments.purpose_student_friendly: Breaks ultraviolet starlight into rainbows to study the chemical composition and temperature of intergalactic gas.
instruments.technical_description: Far-ultraviolet and near-ultraviolet high-throughput spectrograph.

milestones.title: Launch aboard Shuttle Discovery
milestones.description: Deployed into low Earth orbit at an altitude of 600 kilometers.

milestones.title: Historic First Servicing Mission (STS-61)
milestones.description: Spacewalking astronauts installed COSTAR corrective optics, restoring crystal-clear vision.

milestones.title: The Hubble Deep Field
milestones.description: Stared at an empty patch of space for 10 days, revealing thousands of previously unseen distant galaxies.

discoveries.title: Accelerating Expansion of the Universe (Dark Energy)
discoveries.plain_english_summary: By observing distant exploding stars (supernovae), Hubble helped prove that the expansion of the universe is speeding up due to mysterious dark energy.
discoveries.why_it_matters: Fundamentally transformed cosmology, proving that 68% of the universe consists of unknown dark energy.

sources.title: NASA Goddard Hubble Space Telescope Portal
sources.quotation_or_reference: NASA Science Mission Directorate: Hubble Operations

physical_fate: Operating in low Earth orbit (~535 km altitude) travelling at 27,000 km/h, completing an orbit around Earth every 95 minutes. It has made over 1.6 million scientific observations of stars and deep galaxies.
fast_facts: Serviced five times in orbit by spacewalking Space Shuttle astronauts who repaired and upgraded its instruments.
Helped determine that the expansion of the universe is accelerating due to mysterious Dark Energy.
The Hubble Deep Field image revealed thousands of previously invisible galaxies in a patch of sky the size of a grain of sand held at arm's length.
